extracted.intended_audience: licensed customs brokers, broker associations, continuing education providers, and parties seeking to be CBP-selected accreditors
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural rules governing what counts as qualified continuing broker education for customs brokers, how CBP will select and oversee third‑party accreditors, and enforcement/notification procedures tied to certification of completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBP will not act as an accreditor; public-private partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP disagrees with comment requesting that CBP become an accreditor and states that a public-private partnership is necessary to ensure the best qualified continuing broker education opportunities for individual brokers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will select third-party accreditors and provide oversight and a framework for stakeholder input; CBP lacks capacity to vet all potential trainings and prefers private parties to operate within an overseen system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor selection process via SAM/RFI/RFP (contracting-type process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of accreditors will be conducted via SAM and will require a contracting-type process, including response to an RFI and RFP which will produce a binding agreement between the selected party and CBP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM is appropriate and familiar to the public; the RFI/RFP process is intended to be dynamic, responsive, transparent, and produce a diverse pool of accreditors. All potential accreditors must be afforded the same access and opportunity to present credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic accreditor designation; all parties must apply
rubrics_metrics.description: No private party will simply be designated as an accreditor without any review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties wishing to be an accreditor must submit proposals through the RFI/RFP/SAM process and demonstrate credentials; CBP will not recognize specific parties automatically or indefinitely without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor term, renewal, and transparency (initial 3-year term; sunset)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP intends accreditor status to sunset; the first set of CBP-selected accreditors will be approved for three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will publish new RFIs/RFPs to add or replace accreditors as circumstances require; this allows flexibility and the ability to address substandard accreditors and add new ones over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor criteria specified in RFPs, not in regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will not add specific accreditor criteria to the regulations at this time; the criteria for vetting proposals will be outlined in the RFP issued to solicit potential accreditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria may change based on outcomes and experience; codifying detailed criteria in regulation would be too restrictive at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of a licensed customs broker required for accreditor status
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment of a licensed customs broker will be a requirement for a party to be an accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP believes licensed customs brokers have requisite knowledge to vet trainings; CBP may adjust this requirement in future RFIs/RFPs as circumstances dictate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for confidential business information handled via RFP/contract terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about accreditors receiving confidential business procedures should be addressed via the limitations, security expectations, and requirements in the RFPs and contract terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP believes the RFP/contractual conditions and accreditor obligations will prevent inappropriate disclosure; confidentiality protections are better addressed through these mechanisms than in the regulation text itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accreditors accrediting their own trainings (no self-certification)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will prohibit CBP-selected accreditors from accrediting their own training and educational activities to limit conflicts of interest and self-dealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditors may produce training but must not accredit their own offerings; if an accreditor's trainings meet standards, a separate accreditor can reach the same conclusion and accredit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accredit specific trainings/educational activities (not providers) and require pre-accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP and the CBP-selected accreditor will be accrediting specific trainings and educational activities rather than accrediting education providers; continuing broker education credit must be accredited prior to the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-event accreditation will not be allowed because it causes confusion and unpredictability for brokers regarding earned credits; accredited status and number of credits must be clear at time of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor denial reasons and reapplication; prohibition on blanket denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants of denied trainings and educational activities may either reapply or amend an original application; accreditors will provide reasons for denial, and accreditors are prohibited from denying review or approval solely because an activity was previously denied by any CBP-selected accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment to §111.103(d) guarantees flexibility and a pathway for resubmission; specific processes and timeframes will be addressed in the RFPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reaccreditation requirement for trainings and educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP intends requiring all accredited continuing broker education to be reaccredited every year as specified in §111.103(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reaccreditation helps ensure content stays current and prevents circulation of outdated information; CBP disagrees with requests to extend accreditation validity to two or three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-offered trainings qualify if relevant to customs business and CBP will identify them
rubrics_metrics.description: "Training or educational activity offered by another U.S. government agency" will qualify as continuing broker education as long as "the content is relevant to customs business as identified by CBP in coordination with the appropriate U.S. government agency when applicable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will explicitly identify government-offered qualifying events, coordinate with PGAs, assign credit hours, and collect CBP/PGA offerings into an online location on CBP.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized public listings of accreditors and accredited trainings on CBP.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will publish the initial list of available qualified continuing broker education opportunities and maintain a central location on CBP.gov that lists accreditors, links to accreditors' listings, and provides access to CBP and PGA continuing broker education opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditors will also maintain open-access lists tracking every training and educational activity they accredit to allow brokers to confirm validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in defining qualifying education; detailed standards to be developed with accreditors
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will not adopt a more specific definition or prescriptive list of what constitutes qualifying education at this time and believes flexibility is necessary to ensure adequate quantity and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP and CBP-selected accreditors will establish standards and guidelines for continuing broker education after selecting accreditors; additional guidance will be provided later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online and self-guided training allowed if culminating in a retention test (§111.103(a)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP explicitly allows online training and educational activity, whether live or self-guided, that culminates in a retention test to qualify as continuing broker education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change was made to clarify that self-guided online modules are viable sources of continuing education credit and to guarantee a minimum level of participant engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorded presentations or slide decks may qualify only if the entire content is accredited
rubrics_metrics.description: Online training may be offered in recorded format or as slide presentations if the entire recording or slide deck has been approved for continuing education credit by a CBP-selected accreditor; simply recording or recombining content from other accredited activities will not suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific online training must be submitted to an accreditor and accredited; proper documentation must verify completion and that the broker received the training from an accredited source.

rubrics_metrics.name: No continuing education credit for publishing educational materials
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will not award continuing education credit for time spent publishing subject matter for an accredited course or for publishing educational material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP finds awarding credit for publication unworkable and controversial and believes consistent measurement of engagement is not feasible; allowing such credit could create confusion about meeting the 36-credit requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA meetings and federal advisory committee participation excluded from qualifying education
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings conducted in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) are expressly excluded as qualified continuing broker education; participation in committees, subcommittees, workgroups, or other FACA-organized groups does not qualify as training or educational activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FACA meetings are considered advisory or consultative, not educational, and thus do not serve the function of qualifying continuing broker education.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house training can qualify if accredited (no blanket exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP disagrees with commenters seeking to bar in-house company training from eligibility; in-house training may be accredited and thereby provide continuing education credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations and guidance on how in-house training will be evaluated will come after accreditors are selected and standards are developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No required qualifications for presenters of accredited trainings
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will not require that the presenter of an accredited training or educational activity have any specific qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP does not require presenter qualifications for customs broker exam education materials and will apply the same approach for continuing broker education presenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity and fairness in vetting accreditor proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: All potential accreditors must be afforded the same access and the same opportunity to present their credentials during the selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFI/RFP contracting-type process will ensure parity and fair vetting among applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broker certification of completion and record production for enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers must certify completion of the continuing broker education requirement with their triennial status reports; brokers will not be required to attach evidence of the 36 continuing education credits unless CBP requests records under §111.102(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False or misleading statements or material omissions in reports remain enforceable under 19 CFR 111.53(a); failure to certify or to produce requested records can lead to suspension or revocation proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification methods and enforcement timelines (no automated warning; 30-day and 120-day windows; contact methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will not provide automated warning notifications; brokers have 30 days to respond to a notification of potential suspension for failing to certify compliance and 120 calendar days (after suspension) to take corrective action before revocation; CBP will send notifications to an email address if on file, otherwise to a physical address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP considers 30 days a standard response window and 120 days sufficient for extreme situations (e.g., to complete 36 credits). Brokers may verify/update contact information in the ACE Portal; CBP cannot guarantee eCBP Portal missing-field notifications.
